newsitem.title: USA: Merck second-quarter results beat expectations.
newsitem.headline: Merck second-quarter results beat expectations.

text.p: Merck & Co. said Thursday its second-quarter earnings rose a surprisingly strong 19 percent, triggering a sharp rise in its stock, as demand kept growing for its major pharmaceutical products.
The results sparked a rebound in the drug sector as investors recovered from a scare by Pfizer Inc.'s disappointing earnings late Tuesday.
Merck rose $8.25 to $106.75 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was the third most active issue on volume of more than 8 million shares.
Johnson & Johnson rose 37.5 cents to $62.375, Pfizer Inc. climbed $1.06 to $60.31 and Eli Lilly Co. added 50 cents to $114 on the NYSE.
"It was a great quarter for Merck," said Gruntal & Co. pharmaceuticals analyst Adam Greene.
Merck's earnings rose to $1.15 billion from $972.1 million in the year-ago period. Earnings per share jumped 20 percent to 96 cents from 80 cents, 1 cent better than analysts' forecasts.
Sales grew 20 percent to $5.9 billion from almost $5 billion.

For the six months ended June 30, profits climbed 18 percent to 2.2 billion from $1.8 billion. Sales grew 22 percent to $11.5 billion from $9.4 billion, fuelled by stronger sales of blockbuster anticholesterol drug Zocor and other key products.

"Sales growth for the quarter and the first half of 1997 continued to be led by established major products, recent product introductions and the Merck-Medco Managed Care business," said Chairman Raymond Gilmartin in a statement.
"Both our domestic and international operations reported strong unit volume gains."

Foreign exchange fluctuations reduced second-quarter sales growth by 1 percentage point, Merck said. Excluding this effect, sales of Merck human and animal health products grew 15 percent for the quarter.

"Income growth for the first six months was driven by strong unit volume gains," Gilmartin said. "The unfavourable effects of inflation, net of price, and exchange were partially offset by cost controls and productivity improvements in manufacturing, selling and general and administrative expenses."

Greene of Gruntal said he was impressed that Zocor's worldwide sales jumped 25 percent to $865 million in the quarter despite stiff competition from Lipitor, the potent cholesterol fighter launched in February by Warner-Lambert Co.
"Merck alleviated concerns that Lipitor was seriously attacking its franchise in the cholesterol market. That didn't happen because the whole market has expanded," Greene said.

Lipitor, being co-marketed with Pfizer, in recent weeks has captured over 20 percent market share of new prescriptions for anti-cholesterol drugs -- including Zocor and Bristol-Myers Squibb Co.'s Pravachol.
Greene said while Lipitor has chipped away at Zocor's market share, it will likely actually help competitors by increasing overall demand for such drugs.
Other Merck drugs also showed impressive sales growth, analysts said, including osteoporosis drug Fosamax, whose year-on-year sales jumped 92 percent to $127 million.

Sales of the Whitehouse Station, N.J.-based company's ulcer drug Pepcid rose 27 percent in the second quarter to $285 million. Sales of antihypertension drugs Cozaar and Hyzaar, which are sold together, doubled to $161 million.
But sales of Mevacor, another Merck cholesterol-lowering drug, slumped 11 percent in the second quarter to $285 million.
Separately, Merck and Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc. said they plan to close the merger of their animal health and poultry genetics businesses on July 31.

The 50-50 joint venture, Merial Ltd., will be the world's largest company solely dedicated to the discovery, manufacture and marketing of veterinary pharmaceuticals and vaccines, with a revenue base of $1.9 billion and more than 6,000 employees worldwide. Merial is expected to become operational Aug. 1.
